research_question: Can continuous specific conductance and streamflow data be used as effective surrogate regression variables to estimate nitrate concentrations in south-central Idaho springs?

phase_1.user_prompt: I am investigating nutrient pollution and macrophyte growth in six specific springs in Gooding County, Idaho. The springs are: Niagara Springs at Diversion Number 2 near Buhl, Briggs Spring at head near Buhl, Banbury Springs South Vents (08S 14E 33BDD1), Box Canyon Springs near Wendell, Box Canyon Springs below aqueduct diversion near Wendell, and Hatchery Springs Vent17 (08S 14E 06ACC1). Please identify the official USGS site numbers for these six locations. Also, identify the 5-digit USGS parameter codes for electrical conductivity, oxidised inorganic nitrogen as nitrogen, and volumetric flow. We will be focusing on the time period from May 2018 through December 2022.

phase_2.user_prompt: Using the site numbers and parameter codes identified, retrieve all available continuous (high-frequency) and discrete (water quality sample) data for specific conductance, streamflow, and nitrate+nitrite from May 2018 through December 2022.

phase_3.user_prompt: To avoid serial autocorrelation in our regression models, we need to reduce the high-frequency and discrete datasets. For each site, aggregate the specific conductance, streamflow, and nitrate+nitrite data into single monthly means. Merge these into a unified table per site joined by year and month. For Briggs Spring, how many complete monthly observations (rows containing non-null values for all three parameters simultaneously) are available in this aggregated dataset between May 2018 and December 2022?

phase_4.user_prompt: Using the monthly aggregated data for Briggs Spring, build an ordinary least squares (OLS) linear regression model to predict nitrate concentration. Use specific conductance, streamflow, and the harmonic representation of the day of the year (sin(2*pi*day/365.25) and cos(2*pi*day/365.25)) as explanatory variables. What is the adjusted R-squared of this full surrogate regression model? Additionally, create a scatter plot of measured specific conductance versus measured nitrate concentration for Upper Box Canyon Springs to evaluate the linearity assumption. Save this plot as 'upper_box_canyon_linearity.png'.

checkpoint.reference_conclusion: Upper Box Canyon Springs exhibits a non-linear relationship between specific conductance and nitrate at conductance values below approximately 410 µS/cm. The relationship becomes linear and positive at specific conductance values above 410 µS/cm, indicating that specific conductance is only an effective surrogate for nitrate concentrations during periods of higher specific conductance.
checkpoint.visual_description: A scatter plot showing specific conductance on the x-axis and nitrate concentration on the y-axis. The data points should show a flat or highly scattered non-linear cluster at lower specific conductance values (below 410 µS/cm) and a clear positive linear trend at values above 410 µS/cm.
